objective: The importance of security throughout the AI life cycle: business use-case alignment, data collection trustworthiness, model development through deployment and monitoring, and human-centric design (human-in-the-loop, oversight, validation)
secondaryObjectives: The importance of data security in relation to AI: data processing and lineage, data types, watermarking, and retrieval-augmented generation (vector storage, embeddings)

The organization, the systems, the data and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the AI security architect at Tamsin Insurance, a fictional insurer. The data science team is building a model that flags suspicious claims for investigators. You review it at three life-cycle gates.
handover: Training data: five years of claims plus a 'fraud list' scraped from a public forum.
Plan: deploy straight to production and let it auto-deny claims above a score.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Gate 2: testing shows the model flags claims from one repair shop's customers because a competitor posted their names to the forum.
Gate 3: 300 legitimate claims are auto-denied in the first week; customers complain to the regulator.
Gate 4 (follow-up): fraudsters learn the model ignores a new claim pattern; losses rise for two quarters before anyone notices.

choices.label: Drop the scraped list, train on investigator-confirmed outcomes with recorded lineage, and keep a dataset version for each model

effects.log: Training uses traceable, confirmed labels only.

choices.feedback: Training data must be trustworthy and traceable; untrusted labels invite poisoning.

choices.label: Keep the scraped list but spot-check 100 entries
choices.feedback: A spot check can't show the rest wasn't poisoned.

choices.label: Use everything: more data is better
choices.feedback: Anyone who posted to the forum shaped the model.

choices.feedback: Human-centric design keeps people accountable for decisions that affect customers; logs make it auditable.

monPrompt.title: What happens after release
monPrompt.context: Claim patterns change each season; fraudsters adapt.

choices.label: Monitor input drift, score distribution and investigator overturn rate weekly, alert on thresholds, and retrain from versioned data through the same gates

effects.log: Drift and abuse monitoring with triggers is in place.

choices.feedback: A model's security and accuracy decay after release; monitoring and gated retraining keep it trustworthy.

choices.label: Review accuracy once a quarter
choices.feedback: Something, but drift and adaptation can run for months unseen.

choices.label: No monitoring: the model was tested before release
choices.feedback: Pre-release tests say nothing about next season's claims or adapting fraud.

scoring.modelReasoning: Security runs through the AI life cycle: a use case aligned to the business, training data that is trustworthy and traceable (untrusted labels invite poisoning), development and deployment designed around people (models assist, humans decide, everything logged), and monitoring after release for drift and abuse, with retraining through the same gates.
